title: Fleet behavior and execution health (leader + member scorecard)
description: Scorecard for ONE fleet over ONE explicit window, covering three scopes: [fleet] outcome criteria, [leader] conduct of the fleet leader (every leader of record in the window, including successors), and [member] conduct of the member population. GRADING UNIT: subject = the fleet slug (cite it in every evidence string); window = since the previous scorecard for that fleet, capped at 7 days, stated explicitly as UTC start/end. POPULATION: members = every owner_id with a fleet_membership_events row for the fleet (never the live roster alone: ended members drop out of fleet:status); leaders = fleet_role='leader' rows. Member criteria are rated over the POPULATION with rates + a named sample, not one anecdote. EVIDENCE RULES: (1) git commit authorship, commit subjects and Co-Authored-By trailers are NOT evidence of who did what (git-sync commits the whole tree under one identity) — attribute via work-item terminal_owner / completion records / sessions:search; (2) prefer the deterministic queries in each method over judgment; (3) when a census finds zero offending rows, that is a measured healthy, not unknown; (4) rate unknown when the method was not run, and say which step was skipped. RATING ANCHORS: healthy = drift markers absent at the stated thresholds; degraded = drift markers present but bounded (affecting a minority of the population or self-corrected within the window); broken = drift markers systemic (majority of the population, recurring across the window, or causing lost/duplicated work) with no remediation in flight.

criteria.title: [member+leader] Claims flowed without double-placement
criteria.model: Members self-select their next item (claim_next / scheduler:get_next) or are steered by a claim-spec; each item is worked by exactly ONE member at a time. The leader steers via specs/priority as the default; directed placement (hand-assignment) is reserved for flagged needs-dedicated-owner items (see dedicated-ownership-routing) and is always recorded durably on the item. Either way, no two members land on the same item concurrently. A carry-respawn successor resuming its predecessor's item is continuity, not double-placement.
criteria.method: (a) Point-in-time: fleet:status { fleet } members[].doing.id — any item id held by >1 distinct live member is a collision (exclude a predecessor/successor pair of one respawn lineage). (b) Window: for items closed by fleet members in the window, count rows whose worked_by_history holds >=2 DISTINCT fleet-member owner_ids with overlapping claim intervals; report the fraction of closes. (c) coord:orient coverage[] coverage_collisions when available. Report collisions / items-in-flight and name up to 5 examples.
criteria.driftMarkers: coverage_collisions > 0; two live members declaring/holding the same item id; a member idled on a raced claim_next miss while ready work existed; >2% of the window's closes show concurrent multi-member work outside one respawn lineage.

criteria.title: [member] Completion reports were truthful — and all real work has a record
criteria.model: Every terminal transition carries a structured completion that reflects REAL work — filesChanged / root cause, the exact test run + its result, tests added. A truthful 'blocked' is a better outcome than a fabricated all-clear. Fake or recycled 'done' work is the cardinal sin (owner mandate #1). The record must match reality in BOTH directions: no fabricated/inflated reports, AND no GHOST completions — real work landing in the tree with no claim, no thread post, no completion record. Invisible work is a fleet hazard: peers cannot see it, so they re-derive or re-implement it, and its tests may land never-run. Claim-or-post BEFORE implementing; credit follows the record.
criteria.method: (a) Authority census: of the window's closes by fleet members, the share at work_items.authority='committed' vs 'proposed' (proposed = under-evidenced or unowned residue) — dev:pg_query on harness_shared.work_items filtered by terminal_owner IN members and closed_ts in window. (b) Reopen census: share of those closes with a non-empty reopen_history_projection (completion-integrity audit or a peer reopened them). (c) Spot-check >=5 sampled closes via work_items:get: does each cited filesChanged entry exist and contain the claimed change (git show <sha>:<path> content, NOT commit authorship), and does the cited test file exist on a canonical test path? (d) work_items:completion_stats genuineCompletions vs dedupOrUnverified, wave-over-wave. (e) Ghost sweep is content-based only: files changed in the fleet's subsystems during the window that no completion lists — never inferred from git authorship.
criteria.driftMarkers: A completion citing a file/test that does not exist or does not contain the change; a 'passing' claim with no test run; a fabricated state / a send or reading that never happened; authority='proposed' share >5% of closes; reopen share >5%; the completion_stats dedupOrUnverified fraction climbing wave-over-wave with no structural fix; real work landed with no claim/post/completion record; a member's test landed never-run; any attribution argued from git authorship.

criteria.title: [member+leader] Blockers were recorded and escalated, not silently parked
criteria.model: A genuine blocker is recorded durably on the item (work_items:set_blocker with kind/ref/evidence/next action, or set_state=blocked WITH a reason) or escalated to the leader/owner WITH the decision needed — never left as a prose message that scrolls away or an item silently abandoned. A blocker is work to resolve, not just relay: the leader acts on in-scope blockers instead of forwarding them, and a reversible judgment call is parked as a product-decision with a default rather than raised as an owner wall.
criteria.method: (a) dev:pg_query: fleet-held items in status 'blocked' during the window — share with a non-null external_blockers_projection or a blocker reason in payload. (b) harness_shared.coord_open_escalations raised by fleet members/leader in the window (attribute the raiser by joining coord_event_log on msg_id → writer_key): count, age, and whether each names the decision needed. (c) Stalled-silent census: fleet-held non-terminal items with last_progress_at older than 24h and no blocker record. (d) Sample 3 leader-received blockers: did the leader act (fix / route / decide) or only forward?
criteria.driftMarkers: Work stalled >24h with no blocked state and no escalation; a blocker relayed only in chat; an item abandoned mid-flight with no note; a resolvable blocker handed to the owner instead of fixed; escalations naming a problem but no decision; open escalations older than 48h with no owner action requested.

criteria.title: [fleet] Window outcome matched the charter or plan (burn-down, not churn)
criteria.model: The fleet's governing plan items — or, for a standing drain fleet with no plan, its chartered cohort (the claim-spec / scope filter) — reached terminal states consistent with the stated goal; progress is real net burn-down, not churn. A drain whose cohort refills as fast as it closes is treading water, and a high dropped share means the fleet is triaging rather than fixing.
criteria.method: Plan fleets: compare plan item effectiveStatus deltas across the window (plans:items) against the plan ## Now. Drain fleets: count the chartered cohort's open population at window start vs end (work_items:list / dev:pg_query with the charter filter, lane IS DISTINCT FROM 'observation') alongside the fleet's done vs dropped closes; net burn-down = start - end. Quantify churn as cohort items that went wip->todo without reaching a terminal state (per-item recycling is graded under dedicated-ownership-routing / backlog-hygiene).
criteria.driftMarkers: Items churned wip<->todo without terminal progress; the plan ## Now went stale; the window closed with the goal no closer; cohort open count flat or rising despite many closes; dropped share >20% of closes without a stated triage purpose.

criteria.title: [member] Item handoffs were durable — carry-notes, not prose
criteria.model: Parked or handed-off work left a work_items:checkpoint / loop:checkpoint carry-note (what's done / what's left / key insight / gotcha) and, for plan fleets, a plan ## Now pointer, so the next member or the next wake resumes from durable state that survives compaction and respawn. Leader successions are graded under leader-continuity-and-wake-source, not here.
criteria.method: (a) Fleet-held non-terminal items whose holder ended or released in the window: share carrying a checkpoint newer than the last progress (work_items:get checkpoint). (b) Sample 3 carry-respawn or relaunched members: did the successor resume from the checkpoint (no repeated tests, no re-derivation)?
criteria.driftMarkers: A handoff done via a scrolling chat message; no checkpoint on parked or released work; a stale/empty loop carry-note; a member successor reconstructing state from scratch.

criteria.title: [leader] Members alive AND looping, not stranded
criteria.model: Each member is genuinely progressing — its engine loop fires on cadence (auto-wake), it takes turns and pulls work, and it re-arms. A fresh heartbeat is NOT working: a member can hold a fresh heartbeat while its loop is wedged. A parked member between wakes is fine; a member whose loop cannot re-fire, or one stuck in sessionState 'suspect', is stranded and silently stops contributing. Members cannot self-rearm, so the leader detects wedged/stranded/suspect members and wakes them (coord:wake), relaunches truly-ended sessions it still needs, and retires the rest. An intentionally ended loop (deliberate scale-down) is healthy.
criteria.method: fleet:status { fleet }: counts by sessionState (live/parked/suspect/ended) and lastActiveSecAgo distribution; for suspect and long-parked members, loop:status { ownerId } (active, nextFireAt, fireCount, lastDeliveryOutcome, rewake.rewakeGuaranteed). A member alive by heartbeat but loop parked with nextFireAt:null / loop-stuck-backstop is STRANDED. Report stranded+suspect / roster and how long each has been so; check whether the leader acted (wake/relaunch/retire) on members stranded longer than one leader wake interval.
criteria.driftMarkers: Members in 'suspect' or wedged loops for hours with no leader action; members parked far past their interval while ready work sits in the pool; the leader treating heartbeat-alive as working; >10% of the roster stranded/suspect at grading time; recurring stranding with no durable auto-wake fix filed.

criteria.title: [leader] Fleet right-sized to inference / shared-resource capacity
criteria.model: The fleet is sized to the live inference-pool capacity and to the actually-claimable frontier, and does not flood shared resources (the inference gateway, per-account rate limits, the shared box, the shared test runner). The leader scales DOWN under pressure (gateway flooding, 429 account deaths, queue backup) and when the frontier thins, and scales up only into genuine spare capacity AND ready work. A model-specific fleet respects its backend's real quota.
criteria.method: fleet:status headcount { target, current, verdict } and fleet:capacity (dispatchBudget, pool utilization, healthyAccounts, queue depth). Compare executing members with work_items:claimable size for the fleet's charter: members idle with an empty frontier = oversized; frontier waiting with spare capacity = undersized. Watch for 429 / provider-failure system notices naming fleet members in the window. When scaling down su members, confirm loop:end (fleet:cancel/drain are no-ops on su sessions). Count only healthy (non-stranded) members as capacity; stranded seats are graded under member-liveness-and-loop-health.
criteria.driftMarkers: Active members exceed pool capacity (gateway flooding, 429 deaths, queue backup) with no scale-down; members idle or polling an empty frontier; a scale-down that did not reduce load; running a model-fleet into a saturated or owner-killed backend; idle capacity while a ready frontier waits.

criteria.title: [fleet] Completed work actually reached production
criteria.model: A fix that is closed but not LIVE is not done. The window's completed work reaches the running operator: it is committed, promoted and deployed (not frozen behind a stale/red release gate) and not left dark behind an OFF feature flag. A red gate has exactly ONE live fixer (LIVE_GATE_OPS): if that lane is unheld, the leader routes one capable member to it; if it is held by someone else, the fleet sends useful evidence once and keeps working — it never piles members onto the gate.
criteria.method: For a sample of >=5 of the window's closes: dev:pipeline_position { path } on one changed path each (committed -> staging -> main -> deployed). state:read { cell: 'gate.greenCheckpoint.ownership' } and gate verdict for main staleness. Confirm no finished feature from the window ships dark (KNOWN_DARK_FLAGS not grown by the fleet). If the gate was red and unheld during the window, did the leader route exactly one fixer?
criteria.driftMarkers: Completed fixes stuck undeployed (main N commits stale, a red/stalled gate unowned for hours); a finished feature shipped dark; the leader relaying an unowned red gate instead of routing one fixer; 'done' items whose value never reached :3070.

criteria.title: [leader] The claimable pool holds real, actionable, non-duplicate work
criteria.model: Distinct from member-report-integrity (is the COMPLETION real?) — this grades whether the TASKS the fleet draws from are real BEFORE a member burns a turn on them. A healthy pool holds genuine, actionable, correctly-scoped, non-duplicate work: no zombie items (a genuine prior completion that never flipped state, so it resurfaces), no duplicate/auto-synth noise clusters, no items un-executable by the fleet's actual capability (e.g. a 2-machine-rig task for a single-box fleet), and no do-not-claim items recycling because they have nowhere to park. The leader keeps the fleet's slice of the pool clean so claim_next returns doable work.
criteria.method: Start from work_items:claimable { harness } (never a raw status='open' count) restricted to the fleet's charter, lane IS DISTINCT FROM 'observation'. (a) items released by a member as duplicate/already-done/un-doable that remain claimable afterwards; (b) terminal-but-open zombies (terminal_owner + terminal_completion_ref set yet status open/todo); (c) duplicate title clusters and duplicate_of-marked rows still claimable; (d) capability-gated items in a pool the fleet cannot execute. Cross-ref the window's dropped closes: a high share dropped as duplicate/already-done means the pool fed the fleet noise.
criteria.driftMarkers: A member burns a turn discovering an item is a duplicate / already-done / un-doable; an item released as duplicate/already-done/un-doable by one member that is still claimable afterwards; zombie rows accumulate; duplicate clusters grow; capability-gated items sit in the fleet's pool; >10% of the window's closes are drops for duplicate/already-done/not-reproducible.

criteria.title: [leader] Needs-dedicated-owner items get routed, not recycled
criteria.model: Some items are not opportunistic-claimable: fleet-wide-blast-radius changes needing a live controlled verification, converged designs needing a focused multi-file session, owner-gated surfaces. The moment an item is flagged needs-dedicated-owner OR accumulates >=2 investigate-then-release cycles, the LEADER converts it out of the opportunistic pool: directed placement on a named, capable member (coord:dispatch with a brief + a placement comment on the item) or a claim-hold park — never left open for claim_next to hand to holder #N+1. Investigate-then-release WITH a durable handoff note is healthy ONCE.
criteria.method: Deterministic census (dev:pg_query on harness_shared.work_items): items in the fleet's charter touched in the window with last_released_by set AND requeue_count >= 1, or with worked_by_history listing >=3 distinct non-lineage holders. For each hit: is claim_hold set, or is there a placement comment / coord:dispatch naming an assignee? Holders who pulled the item AFTER it was flagged or converged are routing failures. ZERO hits is a measured healthy — do not rate unknown when the census ran and found none.
criteria.driftMarkers: A flagged do-not-claim / needs-dedicated-owner item recycles to a 3rd+ holder; a converged design re-derived from scratch by a later holder; the leader observes ping-pong across wakes without placing or parking it; a placement made only in chat; a placed item silently dropped because the assignee never acked and the leader never followed up.

criteria.title: [member] Communication was economical — no redundant or ceremonial messages
criteria.model: Coordination volume is proportional to coordination need. Members use directed sends with a concrete ask/answer and an explicit expects; broadcasts are reserved for genuinely fleet-relevant state (a shared-tree fault, a gate change) and address @fleet:<slug>, not '*'. No duplicate announcements, no ceremonial ACK chains, no status chatter that a durable surface (work-item state, checkpoint) already carries. A structural fix (claim-spec change, a fact, a plan Decision) beats repeating guidance member-by-member.
criteria.method: coord:catch-up / coord:feed { audience: '@fleet:<slug>' } for the window, or dev:pg_query on harness_shared.coord_event_log filtered to writer_key in the member population and ts in window (recipients in body->'to', disposition in body->>'expects'): messages per terminal close, broadcast ('*') vs @fleet vs directed counts, and the duplicate fraction (same body/summary from >=2 senders or repeated by one sender). dev:coord_categorize buckets the corpus when available. Degraded when messages per terminal close >5 or duplicates >10%; broken when >15 per close.
criteria.driftMarkers: Broadcast '*' used where a directed or @fleet send (or no message) suffices; the same completion/fact announced repeatedly; ACK chains with no content; messages per terminal close >5 or climbing while burn-down stalls; a member narrating each step in chat instead of checkpointing.

criteria.title: [member] Members kept the leader leadable — complete, timely, decision-grade reporting
criteria.model: The leader can steer ONLY on what members surface. Every member's claim, terminal transition (with evidence), blocker (with reason + what was tried), and capacity signal (idle, wedged, rate-limited) reaches the leader through durable surfaces (work-item states, checkpoints, escalations) or a directed send — WITHOUT the leader having to poll each member or re-derive state from raw PG. Escalations name the DECISION needed, not just the problem.
criteria.method: (a) Deterministic: leader tool_invocations in the window of work_items:get / dev:pg_query naming a member-held item (args_json) with no member message to the leader about that item (coord_event_log, body->'to' contains the leader) in the prior 24h — each is a leader-discovered event. (b) Optional judgment sample of the leader's wakes (sessions:search): silent idles, un-escalated blockers, unreported completions the leader had to dig for. Count leader-discovered vs member-reported events. Unanswered directed asks are graded under member-responsiveness-and-stand-down; decision-less escalations under blockers-escalated-not-parked.
criteria.driftMarkers: The leader discovers a member's blocked/idle state by polling, not by report; a completion with no record the leader can see; the leader's picture of member state diverging from live state at every wake.

criteria.title: [member] Context-window usage discipline
criteria.model: Members treat the context window as a managed budget: state is externalized to carry surfaces (facts:assert, work_items:checkpoint, loop:checkpoint) the moment it forms; compaction is deliberate (session:request-compaction at a clean stopping point, before the soft limit); post-compaction resume retrieves (sessions:search / checkpoints) instead of re-deriving; reads are bounded (server-side filters, projection, code:run summaries — no whole-list dumps).
criteria.method: dev:pg_query on harness_shared.coord_event_log for the window: count 'Compaction over-limit' / force-compaction system notices naming member owner_ids, per member and per 100 closes; members with >=2 notices are repeat offenders. Degraded when repeat offenders exceed 10% of the active member population; broken above 30%. Spot-check 2-3 post-compaction members for seamless resume (checkpoint present, no re-derivation churn).
criteria.driftMarkers: Watchdog force-compactions recurring on the same member; post-compaction re-derivation of retrievable state; in-flight work lost at compaction; a member wedged/dead from context exhaustion; unbounded list dumps in transcripts.

criteria.title: [leader] The fleet always had exactly one live, wake-guaranteed leader; successions were deliberate
criteria.model: At every moment of the window the fleet has exactly one leader of record who is live and holds a guaranteed wake source (an armed loop or exact event await), so leadership never silently halts. Leader successions (respawn, handoff, relaunch) are deliberate: the outgoing leader records a carry (charter, constraints, open rulings, member roster state) and the incoming leader resumes from it — no vacancy gaps, no dueling leaders, no lost settings. Frequent successions are themselves a smell: each one re-pays orientation and risks dropped context.
criteria.method: dev:pg_query on harness_shared.fleet_membership_events (fleet_role='leader', event='lead') in the window: distinct leader owner_ids, succession timestamps, and gaps; harness_shared.agent_fleets.leader_missing_since_ms / fleet:status leaderVacant + leaderSessionState. loop:status { ownerId: <current leader> } rewake.rewakeGuaranteed. For each succession, check for a carry (loop carry-note, fact, or work-item checkpoint) dated before the handover.
criteria.driftMarkers: Leader vacancy longer than one leader wake interval; two leaders acting concurrently; a succession with no carry; a charter constraint lost across the succession; >1 succession per day sustained across the window; the current leader with no guaranteed wake source.

criteria.title: [leader] Rulings recorded durably the moment they formed
criteria.model: Any ruling members must follow — a scope call, a do-not-claim, a trade-off, a convention — is recorded where it can be re-read: a plan Decision (plans:add-decision) for plan fleets, a fact (facts:assert) or a comment on the fleet's governing work-item for drain fleets — at the moment it forms. Coord messages relaying a ruling cite its durable id so members re-read the authority instead of trusting a paraphrase. Rulings that change the charter are recorded on the fleet record (agent_fleets.description or a linked plan/fact).
criteria.method: (a) Leader coord sends to members in the window with body->>'expects' = 'action' (harness_shared.coord_event_log where writer_key = a leader owner_id; recipients in body->'to'): sample up to 5 directive-shaped messages and check each cites or creates a durable record (D-NNN, fact key, WI comment). (b) Count plans:add-decision / facts:assert / work_items:comment calls by leaders in the window (harness_shared.tool_invocations by coord_owner_id). Charter EXISTENCE is graded under fleet-charter-and-scope, not here.
criteria.driftMarkers: Rulings only in coord messages; members acting on conflicting paraphrases of one ruling; a ruling re-issued member-by-member instead of recorded once.

criteria.title: [leader] Handoffs and wakes reached a live member, and pickup was verified
criteria.model: When the leader hands work to a member (coord:dispatch / coord:wake / directed send with wake), it reads the delivery result: woken vs recipient_dead vs alive_not_wakeable, and confirms real pickup (the member's progress or reply) rather than trusting woken:1. Ended members are relaunched or retired, never re-woken into a black hole. The leader addresses owners directly instead of relaying through a third member.
criteria.method: Delivery and pickup come from harness_shared.event_wake_deliveries (NOTE workspace_id='default', not the app slug): rows with source = a leader owner_id and subscriber_id = a member, grouped by status (delivered/dropped/dead); turn_proof IS NOT NULL = verified pickup; pickup_escalated_at set = a missed pickup; repeated status='dead' rows for one subscriber_id = waking a black hole. tool_invocations (tool_name IN coord:dispatch / coord:wake / coord:send; args_json->>'to') supplies only the attempt count. For dispatched items, time from dispatch to the item's first progress (work_items.last_progress_at); items with no progress after 2 leader wakes are unverified handoffs.
criteria.driftMarkers: Repeated wakes to ended sessions; dispatched items with no progress after 2 leader wakes and no follow-up; 'handed off' reported without pickup evidence; work relayed through a third agent.

criteria.title: [leader] The leader leads — no babysitting, no hoarding
criteria.model: The leader steers through levers (claim-spec, charter, rulings, placement, capacity) and spends its turns on decisions, not on re-reading unchanged status. It waits on events with one exact await per predicate, never a polling loop beside it; it does not create parallel supervisors; it does not hold implementation items members could take (unless deliberately, with a reason) while members idle. A no-delta wake is short.
criteria.method: Leader tool_invocations in the window: share of calls that are status reads (fleet:status, fleet:assignments, coord:presence, work_items:list/get, state:read) vs actions (dispatch, decide, claim-spec, scale, fix); count consecutive wakes with no action; count events:await + loop:arm on the same predicate. dev:pg_query for items held by leader owner_ids (taken_by) during the window.
criteria.driftMarkers: Leader turns dominated (>70%) by status reads with few actions; a monitor loop plus an await on the same predicate; a parallel supervisor spawned for the same fleet; the leader holding implementation items while members idle on an empty frontier.

criteria.title: [leader+member] The fleet worked its charter and honored owner constraints
criteria.model: The fleet has an explicit charter (which work, which cohort/plan, which exclusions) and owner constraints (e.g. 'non-P2P bugs only', 'no LIVE_GATE_OPS', 'by-ID dispatch only'). Members claim only in-charter work; the leader keeps the claim-spec aligned with the charter and records any change. Out-of-charter work taken without a recorded ruling is drift, even when the work itself was useful.
criteria.method: Derive the charter from the fleet record (agent_fleets.description, linked plan, fleet slug naming, launch kickoff via sessions:search) and scheduler:get_claim_spec. Classify the window's closes and current holds against it with a deterministic filter (e.g. title/scope/tag match for the excluded domain) and report the out-of-charter count and share, with examples. Check owner constraints (e.g. members invoking gate-ops verbs when LIVE_GATE_OPS is excluded) via tool_invocations.
criteria.driftMarkers: No recorded charter; >2% of closes out of charter without a recorded ruling; members working items the leader marked do-not-claim; an owner constraint violated.

criteria.title: [leader] Membership churn proportional to need — stable seats, not identity burn
criteria.model: A fleet seat should be a durable worker: fresh member identities are minted only to replace a genuinely ended seat or to scale into capacity and ready work. Every relaunch re-pays bootstrap and loses warm context, and members that join and end without claiming anything are pure cost. Healthy churn looks like a small multiple of headcount per week; identity burn looks like hundreds of joins against a target of tens.
criteria.method: dev:pg_query on harness_shared.fleet_membership_events for the window: distinct member owner_ids that joined ÷ headcount target (fleet:status headcount.target); joins per day; share of window joiners that never became terminal_owner or taken_by of any work-item (zero-output seats); and the distribution of closes per joiner. Distinguish carry-respawn (same ownerId, continuity) from relaunch (new ownerId).
criteria.driftMarkers: Distinct joiners in the window >3x the headcount target; >30% of joiners with zero claims or closes; joins clustered after mass endings (crash/relaunch loops) with no root-cause item filed; headcount held up by relaunching rather than by keeping seats alive.

criteria.title: [member] Every edit under a held claim; claims and locks respected
criteria.model: A member holds a work-item before its first edit, declares an intent naming it, and closes it with work_items:complete. A claim_conflict means coordinate with the holder, never force; a lock block means pivot or yield, never route around it (rename/copy/sed past the hook). Releases carry a reason.
criteria.method: dev:pg_query: the window's closes by members with first_claimed_at null or taken_by never set (closed without a claim). tool_invocations for members in the window: work_items:claim with force true (args_json->>'force', or the 4th field of args_json->>'row') against an item with a different live taken_by; and work_items:claim error_code='claim_conflict' followed in the window by a work_items:complete on that item by the same member. Lock route-arounds have no ledger today: record 'route-around sub-check not measurable' in the evidence and grade on the measured sub-checks — do not rate unknown for it.
criteria.driftMarkers: Closes on items never claimed; force-claims over a live holder; a complete after a claim_conflict without coordination; a lock route-around (when observable); releases with no reason.

criteria.title: [member] Directed leader asks answered first; stand-down orders obeyed
criteria.model: A directed leader message expecting an answer or action outranks the member's own work: the member replies (or ACKs with an ETA) within its next turn via coord:send, not in its own transcript. A stand-down / yield / scope-change order is followed by the wind-down protocol — finish the atomic step, checkpoint, release with a reason, loop:end, coord:ack — and the member does not keep working after it.
criteria.method: harness_shared.coord_event_log for the window: leader→member messages with body->>'expects' IN ('answer','action') (writer_key = leader, member owner_id in body->'to'); a reply = the member's next message to the leader (body->'to' contains the leader) after the ask — body->>'related_msg_id' is sparse (~3% of rows) and must not be the only linkage, or most replies read as unanswered; report reply rate and latency. For each stand-down order, the member's subsequent tool_invocations (any work after the order = violation) and loop state.
criteria.driftMarkers: Directed asks unanswered for a full wake; answers given only in the member's transcript; members continuing to claim/edit after a stand-down; stand-down without checkpoint/release; >10% of directed asks unanswered.

criteria.title: [member] No pile-on onto singleton lanes (gate, held items, owned incidents)
criteria.model: Some lanes have exactly one owner: the LIVE_GATE_OPS fixer of a red gate, a peer's claimed item, an incident someone already owns. A member that notices one sends useful evidence ONCE to its owner and returns to its own work — no second fixer, no fallback monitor loop, no repeated status reads of a lane it does not own.
criteria.method: harness_shared.tool_invocations for members in the window: distinct members invoking gate-ops verbs (release:checkpoint-run, release:repair-queue, release:deploy) or re-reading gate.greenCheckpoint.* repeatedly; stints by fleet members on the gate-owning work-item (worked_by_history); duplicate investigations of one incident (several members filing/commenting the same root cause).
criteria.driftMarkers: >1 fleet member working a held gate lane; members re-reading gate status every wake; a member arming a monitor on another agent's work; duplicate investigations of one owned incident.

criteria.title: [member] Fixes removed root causes and left a recurrence guard
criteria.model: For bug and drain fleets especially: a close names the root cause (where the wrong behavior originates), lands the durable fix, adds a recurrence guard in the project's canonical test suite, and verifies it — a mitigation is labelled as one and leaves an owned follow-up. bug/capability-gap closes carry completion.rootCauseVerification with distinguishable hypotheses. Closing a bug as 'cannot reproduce' or 'already fixed' cites the evidence that proves it.
criteria.method: Sample >=8 of the window's bug closes via work_items:get: share with a rootCauseVerification block, a named test file on a canonical test path (vitest *.test.ts, playwright e2e, cargo test, llm scenario) that exists in the tree, and a testResult. Reopens are graded under member-report-integrity, not here. Drop-closes: share citing evidence for not-reproducible / already-fixed.
criteria.driftMarkers: Bug closes with no test or an ad-hoc script as the 'test'; restart/retry/widen-timeout fixes closed as done; mitigation without a follow-up item; drop-closes with no evidence.

criteria.title: [member] Filing proportional — residue owned, drain discipline honored
criteria.model: Members file what they discover, deduplicated, with owners: residue is filed with assign_to and listed before the close (no unowned residue); while DRAIN is active members do not mint new items for incidental defects, only for direct blockers to the scoped drain, and keep other evidence on the current item. A fleet whose members file faster than they close is growing the queue it was launched to drain.
criteria.method: dev:pg_query on harness_shared.work_items created by member owner_ids (payload->'_ei'->>'created_by' IN members) in the window: count by kind and lane (observation vs work), share with duplicate_of set, share with first_claimed_at IS NULL at window end (never picked up); compare members' created-work count with their closes (filing ratio). Residue ownership: for sampled closes, every id in completion.verification.coverage.residue had a non-null taken_by at close time (the authority='proposed' share is graded under member-report-integrity).
criteria.driftMarkers: Member work-item filings >= member closes in a drain fleet; >10% of member filings marked duplicates; unowned residue on closes; incidental filings during DRAIN; observation spam (multiple observations per close).
